To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) The orthogonally of AGW normal-mode eigenfunctions is established for waveguides in motion and at rest; 2) A perturbation theory of AGW propagation is developed and used to quantify the relative importance of the gravity and compressibility terms; and 3) The phase and group speeds of normal modes in waveguides are shown to have certain universal characteristics that are independent of the stratification.

(a) The normal modes of a waveguide can be found by solving the eigenvalue problem of a Sturm-Liouville system; (b) The eigenfunctions of the system are orthogonal; and (c) The normal modes can propagate without dispersion if and only if they are Lamb waves.

AGWs can be guided by a waveguide with a piecewise continuous profile of the flow velocity, sound speed, and density.
